summary: This note is a documentation page for the CURRENT_STATEMENT function, which returns the SQL text of the statement currently executing. It shows the syntax CURRENT_STATEMENT() with no arguments and gives one example where a SELECT query returns its own text as output. The page is a clipped web page, and its navigation and footer boilerplate has been ignored.
one_line: Reference page for the CURRENT_STATEMENT() SQL function, which returns the text of the currently executing statement.
key_facts: CURRENT_STATEMENT returns the SQL text of the statement that is currently executing.
The syntax of CURRENT_STATEMENT is CURRENT_STATEMENT() with no arguments.
CURRENT_STATEMENT takes no arguments; the page lists Arguments as 'None.'
The example query is SELECT 2.71, CURRENT_STATEMENT();
In the example output, the CURRENT_STATEMENT() column contains the text 'SELECT 2.71, CURRENT_STATEMENT();'.
The example output column for 2.71 has the value 2.71.
The page is listed under the Categories section of the documentation.
The page's sections include Syntax, Arguments, and Examples.
